chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: عَنْ حَمْدَوَيْهَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ يُونُسَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Hammad who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَأْمُرُ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ حَكِيمٍ أَنْ يُجَالِسَ أَهْلَ الْمَدِينَةِ فِي مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَيُكَلِّمَهُمْ وَيُخَاصِمَهُمْ حَتَّى كَلَّمَهُمْ فِي صَاحِبِ الْقَبْرِ وَكَانَ إِذَا انْصَرَفَ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ: مَا قُلْتَ لَهُمْ وَمَا قَالُوا لَكَ وَيَرْضَى بِذَلِكَ مِنْهُ

translations.en: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to order Muhammad ibn Hukaym to sit with the people of Madina in the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and talk to them and debate with them – such that he even debated with them regarding the companion of the grave – and when he used to go to meet him, he would ask: 'How did you argue with them? How did they argue with you?' and he used to be pleased with that from him.

en.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the strategic role of Muhammad ibn Hukaym as a key theological debater during the era of Imam al-Rida (AS), emphasizing the Imam's active mentorship in refining his companion's rhetorical skills. The specific mention of debating the 'Sahib al-Qabr' (often identified as the Qaramita or early Shia opponents regarding the occultation or burial sites) underscores the historical context of defending core Shia doctrines in public forums. This interaction illustrates the scholarly tradition of 'munazara' (debate) as a means of establishing religious authority and clarity for the community.
en.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida (AS) evaluate the debating skills of his companion Muhammad ibn Hukaym?

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْقَبْرِ: The companion of the grave (referring to Abu Bakr)
